hypothesis: Large between-prompt directions in response features may encode shared content that distracts author attribution; removing a few may help unseen-prompt classification.
evidence_status: Our untested truncated prompt-mean PCA hypothesis, not a LEACE replication or guaranteed concept erasure.
source_connection: LEACE relates concept means/cross-covariance to linear erasure and warns of collateral damage. Its oblique optimal erasure differs from our fixed-rank orthogonal PCA projection. No cited evidence establishes a gain on this competition.
features: Existing independently fitted V34 8B CE outer folds 1-4 plus original V25 pilot fold 0; no new backbone training
projection: Per layer, average raw features within each complete 18-author training prompt; centre these equally weighted means, take top right singular vectors, remove selected subspace from each row. Exclude incomplete prompts only from PCA; retain every training row in classifier fitting. No validation means or labels enter fitting.

readout.method: Train-only StandardScaler then multinomial logistic regression; mean per-layer log probabilities, unchanged historical specification

metrics: pooled and per-fold balanced accuracy of raw neural classifier
secondary fixed V34 sparse plus .15 neural score blend with unchanged per-fold balancing
rank0_parity: Report cached score differences and prediction disagreements per fold. All hypothesis gains measured only against the refitted local rank0 control, never the cached Kaggle predictions.
inference: Single text feature uses stored mean and projection then readout; no prompt ID or other responses needed
limits: Exploratory repeatedly examined development CV, including reused pilot; not untouched confirmation
No rank selection or gates changed during run
No full-incumbent ensemble validation or leaderboard gain claim
No GPU, API generation or spending
Projection may erase author information intertwined with content
